title: Governor Generals Of Bengal
definition: The official designation established by the Regulating Act of 1773, elevating the Governor of Bengal to Governor-General of Bengal with supervisory control over the Presidencies of Madras and Bombay, functioning as the chief executive administrator of British East India Company territories in India until the Charter Act of 1833 transformed the office into the Governor-General of India.
importanceInUpsc: This microtopic forms the bedrock of Modern Indian History and Constitutional Development in the UPSC Civil Services Exam. Questions regularly test the statutory evolution of executive authority, administrative reforms, judicial reorganizations, and land revenue settlements introduced during their tenures in both Prelims (chronology, acts) and Mains (imperial consolidation, economic drain, administrative centralization).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and statutory mechanisms of the Governor Generals of Bengal from 1773 to 1833.
Evaluate spatial distribution, administrative frameworks, judicial reforms, and land revenue settlements.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims chronology and match-the-following questions.
prerequisites: Carnatic Wars and Battle of Plassey/Buxar
Dual Government system of Robert Clive
